High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7701 of 2023
Applicant :- Rajendra

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Dhirendra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri R.C. Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant submits that on 31.3.2023 he has filed power on behalf of applicant in the registry but his name could not be shown in the cause list.

2. Heard Sri R.C. Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Varun Kumar Agnihotri, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
142 of 2022, under Sections 302, 201, 498A IPC, Police Station- Badgaon, District- Saharanpur,
during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. F.I.R. of the present case was lodged against applicant and four others and according to the F.I.R.
marriage of the applicant was performed with the daughter of informant about 7-1/2 years before and applicant and his family members used to torture the daughter of informant for want of dowry and on 3.8.2022 applicant and other accused persons committed the murder of the daughter of informant and without informing him disposed off her body.

5. Learned counsel for applicant submits that entire allegation made against applicant is totally false Rajendra vs State Of U.P. on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188739547/
1 and frivolous and applicant neither demanded any dowry nor he ever tortured deceased and actually deceased i.e. his wife committed suicide and immediately after the incident he informed the informant and after receiving information informant arrived at his home and also participated in the funeral proceedings but subsequently he lodged F.I.R. of the present case after cooking up a false story.
6. He next submits even from perusal of F.I.R. and the statement of the informant, it appears that entire allegation with regard to demand of dowry is totally false as neither in the F.I.R. nor in the statement any specific demand of dowry was disclosed and in the F.I.R. only it is mentioned that for dowry applicant and his family members tortured the deceased and in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. informant stated that for additional demand his daughter was being tortured by applicant and others and, therefore, allegation with regard to demand of dowry appears to be vague.
7.

Learned counsel for applicant further submits the present matter is not a case under Section 304B IPC rather it is a case under Section 302 IPC and, therefore, no presumption can be drawn against applicant and even if applicant after the death of his wife without informing the informant disposed off her body then he cannot be held liable for murder of his wife and he can only be punished under Section 201 IPC for concealment of evidence.
8. He further submits applicant in the present matter is in jail since 1.9.2022 i.e. for last more than seven months.

9. Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is the husband of the deceased and without informing the informant after death in hurry he disposed off her body and this fact clearly suggests that after committing her murder he did the cremation.

Learned A.G.A. further submitted that although presumption under Section 113 B India Evidence Act cannot be raised against applicant but applicant is the husband of the deceased and in hurry he disposed off the body of his wife and he failed to provide any plausible explanation in this regard that why he did the cremation in hurry and why his wife committed suicide and, therefore,
presumption against him can very well be drawn under Section 106 Indian Evidence Act.
9. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. It appears that applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances but beyond seven years of her marriage and although applicant submits that the information of death of his wife was furnished by him to the informant but from perusal of the material available on record it appears that without informing him he did the cremation. However,
as present matter is of Section 302 IPC, therefore, no presumption can be drawn against applicant under Section 113B Indian Evidence Act but as applicant is the husband and he failed to provide and plausible explanation of the death of his wife and from the record it is apparent that he in hurry without informing informant disposed off the body of his wife, therefore, presumption under Section 106 Indian Evidence Act can be drawn against him.
Rajendra vs State Of U.P. on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188739547/
2 11. Therefore, considering the conduct of the applicant and particularly the fact that he failed to disclose the reason of the death of his wife, in my view, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected at this stage.

Order Date :- 19.4.2023 Kumar Manish.
